name: Glitch
description: A buffer that misbehaves by chance: slices of what you play are repeated, stuck like a scratched disc, reversed or slowed to a stop, as hard cuts or as soft stumbles.

params.name: Time
params.description: Length of the slices the sound is cut into. Short slices stutter and buzz; long ones repeat or reverse whole phrases.

params.name: Chance
params.description: How often a slice goes wrong. At zero nothing ever happens and the sound passes untouched; at full every slice is a glitch.

params.name: Repeat
params.description: How likely a glitch is to be a repeat, where the last slice plays again up to eight times. It is weighed against Skip, Reverse and Slow.

params.name: Skip
params.description: How likely a glitch is to be a skip, where the sound jumps back and sticks on a tiny fragment like a scratched disc.

params.name: Reverse
params.description: How likely a glitch is to play the last slice backwards.

params.name: Slow
params.description: How likely a glitch is to slow the sound down: either it drops to half speed, or it winds down to a stop like a tape machine and spins back up.

params.name: Calm
params.description: Softens every glitch. At zero they are hard digital cuts that click; turned up they fade in and out and get darker, until they are gentle stumbles and smears.

params.name: Decay
params.description: Makes each repeat quieter and darker than the one before, so a stuck slice dies away instead of hammering.

params.name: Bounce
params.description: Makes each repeat shorter than the last, so the repeats speed up like a dropped ball coming to rest.

params.name: Octaves
params.description: Chance that a repeated or stuck fragment plays an octave up at double speed, or an octave down at half speed.

params.name: Spread
params.description: Throws each glitch to a random place left or right of centre. Zero leaves them where the sound was.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the untouched sound and the glitched one. Below full, what you play stays audible underneath each glitch.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Models in outline the faults of a skipping disc player and of a sampler whose buffer misbehaves (repeat, stuck loop, reverse, half speed, tape stop), chosen by a seeded random draw at each slice; it is not taken from a paper or a circuit. Splices are raised-cosine crossfades; double-speed reads go through a short half-band low-pass with a Kaiser window (after the approach of J. F. Kaiser, 'Nonrecursive digital filter design using the I0-sinh window function'); all other reads use Catmull-Rom interpolation.
